propertyEvents.locator: Register!A8:Q33 and Other Entries!A8:D9; the year’s depreciation and the entries to accumulated depreciation

propertyEvents.result: The 12 monthly depreciation entries booked $451,600.00, a flat twelfth each month; the register’s FY2026 depreciation is $424,700.00. propertyEvents.result: Test 26-01261 (AJ-26-0633), the top-side revenue entry
propertyEvents.locator: PDF pages 1 and 2; the Controller’s and the Chief Financial Officer’s answers

propertyEvents.result: 26-01261 debits account 1300 and credits Pier 9 revenue $48,000.00, “Revenue earned in June, Pier 9 CO-07 seismic hold-down work, per the p”. It is dated June 30 but was posted on Saturday, August 8 at 9:41 PM, five days after June was closed: the period was never locked (LOCK-01). It was set to reverse, and did, on July 2, 2026 (27-00006). Nothing supports it: the June 30 schedule’s under billings are $61,250.00, and with the entry account 1300 is $109,250.00. The Controller says the project manager’s estimate is to follow; the Chief Financial Officer did not know of it. Revenue and account 1300 are overstated by $48,000.00 (TOP-01).
propertyEvents.locator: PDF pages 1 and 2; the Controller’s and the Chief Financial Officer’s answers

propertyEvents.locator: Entries!A8:N, Lines!A8:H, Control Totals!A8:E and After Year End!A8:I; every FY2026 entry and line, the system’s totals and the reversals after June 30

propertyEvents.result: 6 entries dated July 1 to August 31, 2026 reverse an FY2026 entry. 5 are the accruals the policy marks to reverse on the first day of the next period: the June 30 accrued wages and the year-end accrued expenses, warranty reserve, bonuses and premium audit, $600,593.69. The other is 27-00006, reversing 26-01261 on July 2, a date the policy does not use, so that FY2026 keeps the $48,000.00 and FY2027 gives it back.

propertyEvents.result: Read management’s answers about the entries and the pressures on the year
propertyEvents.locator: PDF pages 1 and 2; the Controller’s and the Chief Financial Officer’s answers

propertyEvents.result: Dana Whitfield: the entry was booked “so June revenue matched what he expected”, and she does not have the estimate. Jordan Hale: he was asked to approve no year-end entry and did not know of it. And the covenants are tested on the June 30 statements; the compliance certificate went to the bank on August 10, two days after the entry. Whether this is an override of controls is the CPA’s question to the officers (OVR-01); the machine does not decide intent.

Ready for the CPA
Set what was found against materiality
propertyEvents.locator: Entries!A8:N, Lines!A8:H, Control Totals!A8:E and After Year End!A8:I; every FY2026 entry and line, the system’s totals and the reversals after June 30

propertyEvents.result: One known misstatement: $48,000.00 of unsupported revenue (TOP-01), 14.1% of materiality, above the clearly trivial $17,000.00. In amount it is small; in kind it is not: a manual revenue entry by the person who closes the books, after the close, at night, unsupported and set to reverse. With JE-01, LOCK-01, SELF-01 and LIST-01 it is what the CPA weighs for management override. The trial balance every FY2026 area read does not hold it; the ledger does. The machine stops here.
propertyEvents.locator: Entries!A8:N, Lines!A8:H, Control Totals!A8:E and After Year End!A8:I; every FY2026 entry and line, the system’s totals and the reversals after June 30

log.detail: 06 Inquiries/Journal entry inquiries with management.pdf PDF pages 1 and 2; the Controller’s and the Chief Financial Officer’s answers

log.text: 26-01261 debits account 1300 and credits Pier 9 revenue $48,000.00, “Revenue earned in June, Pier 9 CO-07 seismic hold-down work, per the p”. It is dated June 30 but was posted on Saturday, August 8 at 9:41 PM, five days after June was closed: the period was never locked (LOCK-01). It was set to reverse, and did, on July 2, 2026 (27-00006). Nothing supports it: the June 30 schedule’s under billings are $61,250.00, and with the entry account 1300 is $109,250.00. The Controller says the project manager’s estimate is to follow; the Chief Financial Officer did not know of it. Revenue and account 1300 are overstated by $48,000.00 (TOP-01).

log.text: One known misstatement: $48,000.00 of unsupported revenue (TOP-01), 14.1% of materiality, above the clearly trivial $17,000.00. In amount it is small; in kind it is not: a manual revenue entry by the person who closes the books, after the close, at night, unsupported and set to reverse. With JE-01, LOCK-01, SELF-01 and LIST-01 it is what the CPA weighs for management override. The trial balance every FY2026 area read does not hold it; the ledger does. The machine stops here.
